No way to silence the `litmodels` advertisement

### Bug description

```
💡 Tip: For seamless cloud uploads and versioning, try installing [litmodels](https://pypi.org/project/litmodels/) to enable LitModelCheckpoint, which syncs automatically with the Lightning model registry.
``` 

This advertisement is displayed even if `litmodels` is installed, but not used.

I don't need any "cloud uploads and versioning". In fact, I am often working with proprietary models and restricted data. I sincerely hope that this "tip" isn't suggesting that `lightning` is going to automatically upload anything anywhere (whether I have this `litmodels` package installed or not).

Please, do one of the following (in order of personal preference):
1) remove this advertisement
2) only show this advertisement when appropriate (perhaps, if you detect that the user does have `litmodels` installed or is already using some "cloud"-related stuff)
3) provide a way to silence this advertisement

### What version are you seeing the problem on?

v2.5

`LearningRateFinder` fails due to missing `weights_only` parameter in checkpoint restore

### Bug description

  ## Summary
`LearningRateFinder` fails when restoring its internally created temporary checkpoint because it does not expose or forward a `weights_only` parameter.  
Since PyTorch ≥ 2.6 defaults to `weights_only=True` for `torch.load`, Lightning attempts a *weights‑only* load on a checkpoint that contains full module objects, causing an `UnpicklingError`.

Manual checkpoint loading works correctly when `weights_only=False` is explicitly passed.

This makes `lr_find()` unusable for any model whose checkpoint includes non‑trivial Python objects (e.g., custom modules).

---

 ## Environment
- PyTorch: 2.12.x
- Lightning: 2.4.x
- Python: 3.11
- OS: Windows (Jupyter environment)

FLOPs numbers are inconsistent

### Bug description

The FLOPs numbers in [throughput.py](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/master/src/lightning/fabric/utilities/throughput.py) for H100 and H200 GPUs have some inconsistencies that have caused me some confusion when switching between GPU types: 

- all H200 and the H100 NVL GPU seem to be using sparse FLOPs numbers 
- the H100 SXM and PCIE models seem to using dense FLOPs, see: https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-gpu-resources/h100-datasheet-24306

I think it would be good to standardize on one and also document the behaviour as there's a factor 2 difference between the two.

master

tasks.prompt:
Improved control of device stats callbacks

## Proposed refactor
Separate device stats monitoring into separate callbacks per-device, but sub-class from `DeviceStatsMonitor`. This preserves the desired change from #9032 to consolidate the interface, but also allows for fine-grained control.

### Motivation
With #9032, all the accelerators were combined under a single `DeviceStatsMonitor` callback. This consolidated the API, but it also removed fine-grained control. For instance, the `GPUStatsMonitor` that is now being deprecated used to provide fine-grained control over the `nvidia-smi` stats that were tracked.

However, the new interface defaults to using torch memory stats (which provide less info than nvidia-smi).

Regardless of whether GPU stats are changed to default to `nvidia-smi`, the user no longer has control over what metrics are monitored. The proposed refactor would allow users to use `CPUStatsMonitor`, `GPUStatsMonitor`, etc. as before, while also keeping the consolidated `DeviceStatsMonitor` API.
